title: K Smallest in Stream, Original Order
statement:
You are given an array of `n` integers and an integer `k`. Select the `k` smallest elements of the array and print them **in the order in which they appear in the array** (not sorted by value).

When equal values compete for the last places, the one that appears **earlier** in the array is preferred. Formally, rank the elements by `(value, index)` in ascending order, keep the first `k`, and print the kept elements by increasing index.

**Follow-up:** now the numbers do not come as a fixed array but as a continuous stream. At any moment you must be able to report the `k` smallest numbers seen so far, in the order they arrived, using only `O(k)` memory. (Only the fixed-array version is tested.)
inputFormat:
The first line contains two integers `n` and `k`.
The second line contains `n` integers, the array.
outputFormat: Print the `k` selected values on one line, separated by single spaces, in their original order.

examples.explanation: Ranked by (value, index): (1, 3), (2, 1), (2, 5), (4, 7), ... The first three are the values at indices 3, 1 and 5. Printed by increasing index they are 2 (index 1), 1 (index 3), 2 (index 5).
All values tie, so the earlier indices 0 and 1 are kept.
With k = n every element is kept, in original order.

hints: Sorting the whole array loses the original positions. Think about how to remember each element's index.
Keep a max-heap of size k holding (value, index): when it grows beyond k, drop the largest, so the heap always holds the k smallest elements seen so far.
After the scan, order the heap's elements by index to restore the original order. The same heap handles a stream, since it never needs the full input.
